description: Committee recommends 2027 budget with 6.09% property tax increase.
Includes $68.9M for roads, $67.8M for police, $76.2M for fire.
Adjustments could lower 2027 tax increase to 5.45%.

chips.text: Recommended
2027 property tax supported civic budget is $718.1 million.

description: Resident Frank Regier highlighted struggles with rising city costs.
He suggested cutting high city management wages.

chips.text: Recommended
Public delegate expressed deep concern over rising costs pushing residents to homelessness.
Rising costs disproportionately impact low-income residents

speakers.name: Frank Regier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Budget Issue
said: High taxes push people to homelessness, food banks, and difficult choices.
Current budget proposals are too high; council must do better.
Recommends cutting high manager wages to reduce city spending.

description: Committee recommends city fund over $30,000 for two festivals.
These free events attract 72,000+ people downtown.
Organizations manage Canada Day celebrations for city.

chips.text: Recommended
Nutrien Fireworks Festival has a total budget of $2.5 to $3 million.
28% of fireworks festival attendees are Saskatoon visitors.
Residents value downtown festivals for accessibility and cultural representation.
Festivals provide a sense of safety and acceptance for newcomers.

speakers.name: Nowshad (Shad) Ali
speakers.organization: On Purpose Leadership Inc. and Saskatoon Fireworks Festival Inc.
said: Proposed budget charges significantly impact Canada Day and Fireworks Festival.
Festivals provide unique social, economic, and tourism benefits.
Other funding avenues are insufficient; city should cover full costs.

description: Committee recommends 2027 budgets for three city corporations.
TCU Place, SaskTel Centre project operating surpluses.
Remai Modern requests 2% operating grant; all include capital.
No new staff positions are requested.

chips.text: Recommended
SaskTel Centre plans $910,000 capital spending for 2027.
SaskTel Centre discussed 'blue dot fever' and high ticket prices impacting sales.
Downtown Saskatoon hotels, restaurants, and small businesses depend on TCU Place events.
Remai Modern commits to featuring Indigenous artists in every programming season.
Remai Modern faces 50% tariffs on proprietary lighting system materials, risking capital budget.
Remai Modern integrates Indigenous perspectives and culture throughout its organization.
Remai Modern plans to bring more art into public spaces with the city.

description: Saskatoon Public Library's 2027 operating budget of $38.3M is recommended.
A $500,000 capital budget for equipment replacement is recommended.
Operating budget includes $192,300 more from assessment growth.

chips.text: Recommended
That the 2027 Operating Plan approved by City Council on November 25, 2025
Proposed 2027 levy increase is $1,841,300 or 5.22%.

Councillor Dubois asked if SPL would seek provincial funding for security; staff had no plans.
Library supports youth, newcomers, and marginalized residents with inclusive services.
New central library expected to open by fall 2027.

description: Recommends approving Saskatoon Police Service's $149.9 million 2027 budget.
Budget includes 33 new full-time positions.
Funds transit policing and provincial SCAN programs.
Estimated 2.2% mill rate impact for taxpayers.

chips.text: Recommended
2027 budget is $149.9 million, a $7.7 million increase from 2026.
Councilors advocated for in-house police training to address college capacity and reduce overtime.
Transit riders and operators benefit from increased safety and bylaw enforcement.
Single parents face barriers to policing careers due to 22-week off-site training requirements.
Chief committed to reducing unprecedented overtime and making policy changes in 2027.

description: Proposes 39.5 new 2027 staff for rapid transit.
Adds 6.5 new 2027 staff for fire and risk reduction.

chips.text: Recommended

description: Funds coordinated safety plans to address social disorder.
Allocates $300,000 from reserves for 2027 plan operations.

chips.text: Anticipated cost for 2027 coordinated safety plans is $459,000.
City administration states province views community safety as a municipal responsibility.

Business Improvement Districts are involved in plan building and feedback.

description: Saskatoon Fire requests 12 new staff to fully crew all fire trucks.
This prevents one fire truck from being out of service often.

chips.text: Hiring 12 firefighters increases the budget by $1.3 million annually.
Council inquired about ongoing SHA negotiations for EMS call reimbursement.
Firefighters' wellness is impacted by current high overtime usage.

description: Extends Indigenous Support Team pilot until December 2027 for $220,000.
Team connects vulnerable people to downtown services.

chips.text: Extension costs $31,500 monthly for high-activity periods, $25,000 for original pilot.
Councillor Tomo questioned using RCE for a second pilot, citing governance concerns.
Vulnerable individuals in the Riversdale BIDs area are supported.
Administration will propose bylaw revisions to allow RCE funding for future pilots.
Specific feedback from BIDs on the Indigenous Support Team's presence remains unclear.
Community members expressed not seeing the Indigenous Support Team on patrol.
Team provides culturally responsive support to vulnerable Indigenous individuals.
Staff promised to provide council and partners with performance data and updates.

description: City proposes adding staff to Shakespeare on Saskatchewan washrooms.
Aims to reduce 5,500 hours of closures from vandalism.
Requires $75,000 capital; $245,500 annual cost impacts taxes 0.07%.

chips.text: Capital funding of $75,000 could come from RCE funding.
Councillor asked about access controls like QR codes instead of human monitoring.
Administration has not specifically looked into access controls like QR codes for washrooms.
Staff will report back on alternative washroom monitoring options before next budget.

description: Council reviewed city's community grant programs for 2027 budget.

chips.text: Station 20 received $62,000 (2025) and $69,000 (2026) in tax abatements.

description: Recommend $1,938,000 for 2027 capital projects.
Includes funding for community safety and Indigenous support.

And riverbank washroom monitoring program.

chips.text: Recommended

Councillor Pierce opposed Indigenous Support Team
Safety plan and Indigenous support aim to help unhoused and vulnerable residents.
